newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Senator says less likely to vote for Telstra.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Senator says less likely to vote for Telstra.

text.p: Key Australian independent senator Brian Harradine said on Friday that he was now slightly more likely to vote against the government's proposed one-third privatisation of telecoms carrier Telstra Corp.
On Thursday, Communications Minister Richard Alston said he expected job cutting by Telstra in Harradine's home state of Tasmania would be greater than he first thought.
Harradine said those job losses would occur regardless of the sale of Telstra.
"Even if I voted against the sale of Telstra, which is a little more likely following yesterday, then the job losses would still take place, unfortunately," Harradine told reporters.
He had not, however, decided how he would vote.

Alston's correction made him more sceptical of assurances he had received from Telstra, he said. "I am very sceptical, to be quite frank, about the details that are currently being given to me which are sourced from Telstra," he said.
"One has to question the credibility of those figures."

The government needs the support of Harradine and another Independent, Mal Colston, for the upper house of parliament, the Senate, to pass the legislation authorising the privatisation, which is supposed to raise about A$8 billion.
